title: Evaluating what unsupervised STDP learns: code, configurations and run maps
description:
Code, configurations and run-selection maps for the paper Evaluating what unsupervised STDP learns: matched random baselines, linear readouts, and a controlled reappraisal of three plasticity rules (Abin S and Raji Susan Mathew).

The paper compares three STDP rules: pair-STDP (Diehl and Cook), triplet-STDP (Pfister and Gerstner) and voltage-STDP (Clopath et al.). Each rule trains a competitive, fully connected spiking layer of 400 neurons. Every trained network is compared with the same network with STDP disabled (the matched random baseline), and is read out with a linear probe as well as the usual post-hoc labelling. The comparison covers eight datasets: MNIST, N-MNIST, EMNIST-Letters, Fashion-MNIST and four MedMNIST sets. Controls include a two-layer convolutional network and an exact reimplementation of Clopath's neuron and update rule. The same matched random baseline is also applied to SoftHebb (Journé et al., 2023), a recent Hebbian method, on CIFAR-10 and four medical datasets.

Trained weights, run outputs and datasets are not included; README.md and RUN_MAP.md say how to regenerate each table and figure. SoftHebb's code and Clopath's MATLAB code are not redistributed; README.md says where to obtain them.
